concept.name: Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring
concept.title: Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring

spark.summary: Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Scoring combines millisecond sliding-window velocity counters with 2-hop entity-ring graph traversal to block payment fraud before funds settle.
spark.keyTakeaway: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, velocity counters catch individual card-testing bursts, while 2-hop Device/IP/Card graph lookups expose coordinated fraud rings rotating stolen credentials.
spark.byteSummary:
Modern payment fraudsters bypass simple static rules by distributing attacks across hundreds of stolen cards, rotating residential proxies, and mimicking normal checkout pacing.

Streaming Fraud Detection pairs two complementary real-time signals under a strict 30ms SLA: Stateful Velocity Counters in Apache Flink (tracking 5m, 1h, and 24h spend and attempt counts per card, device, and IP) and a Graph Engine executing 2-hop neighborhood lookups to detect shared devices or mule accounts.

These features feed a Hybrid Ensemble—combining deterministic compliance rules with an XGBoost + GNN risk model—producing a 0–1000 score that routes transactions to Approve, Step-Up 3DS, or Hard Block.

learningJourney.title: Why Rules-Only Fraud Systems Fail
learningJourney.purpose: Understand false-positive friction vs. adversarial rule evasion.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Why Rules-Only Fraud Systems Fail** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Understand false-positive friction vs. adversarial rule evasion.
explanation.core: Static thresholds like 'block if amount > $500 and country != home' create high false positives for legitimate travelers while missing low-dollar card-testing attacks ($1.00 probes). Scoring requires continuous behavioral context across time and linked entities.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, why rules-only fraud systems fail becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production fraud scoring architecture with champion-challenger shadow logging, 1% audit holdouts, and 3DS-proxy adversarial drift detection.

learningJourney.title: Stateful Sliding-Window Velocity Counters
learningJourney.purpose: Compute 5m, 1h, and 24h transaction bursts in Flink RocksDB.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Stateful Sliding-Window Velocity Counters** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Compute 5m, 1h, and 24h transaction bursts in Flink RocksDB.
explanation.core: Card-testing bots fire 20–50 small authorizations within minutes. Flink maintains keyed sliding-window counters (5m, 1h, 24h) per card_hash, device_id, and ip_subnet in RocksDB, updating incrementally in <2ms without scanning raw history.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, stateful sliding-window velocity counters becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production fraud scoring architecture with champion-challenger shadow logging, 1% audit holdouts, and 3DS-proxy adversarial drift detection.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, velocity counters catch individual card-testing bursts, while 2-hop Device/IP/Card graph lookups expose coordinated fraud rings rotating stolen credentials.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.

learningJourney.title: 2-Hop Graph Ring Lookup
learningJourney.purpose: Expose coordinated fraud rings sharing devices, cards, or payout accounts.

explanation.foundation: Think of **2-Hop Graph Ring Lookup** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Expose coordinated fraud rings sharing devices, cards, or payout accounts.
explanation.core: Fraudsters rotate cards across one emulated device or reuse a single mule bank account across 50 identities. A real-time Graph Engine executes a 2-hop traversal (Card -> Device -> Other Cards) in <8ms to count linked chargebacks and ring density.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, 2-hop graph ring lookup becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production fraud scoring architecture with champion-challenger shadow logging, 1% audit holdouts, and 3DS-proxy adversarial drift detection.

learningJourney.title: Cost-Sensitive Threshold Calibration
learningJourney.purpose: Tune Approve/3DS/Block thresholds based on dollar fraud loss vs. false-decline cost.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Cost-Sensitive Threshold Calibration** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Tune Approve/3DS/Block thresholds based on dollar fraud loss vs. false-decline cost.
explanation.core: Blocking a $2,000 legitimate order costs margin and customer lifetime value, while missing a $20 fraud costs $20 + chargeback fee. Expected-cost thresholding sets dynamic cutoffs per transaction value rather than using a single fixed probability.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, cost-sensitive threshold calibration becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production fraud scoring architecture with champion-challenger shadow logging, 1% audit holdouts, and 3DS-proxy adversarial drift detection.

learningJourney.title: Handling 60-Day Delayed Chargeback Labels
learningJourney.purpose: Train models accurately when true fraud labels arrive weeks after the transaction.

explanation.foundation: Legitimate cardholders often take 30–60 days to dispute a fraudulent charge.
explanation.core: Training on yesterday's data falsely labels undetected fraud as legitimate.
explanation.deepDive: We use a 45-day label maturity window combined with immediate human-analyst case labels.

cards.detail: Never treat an un-disputed 2-day-old transaction as a confirmed good order.

cards.label: Importance Weighting
cards.detail: Weight recent analyst-reviewed cases to adapt to new attack vectors.

sectionDiagram.summary: Maturity windows prevent un-reported recent fraud from contaminating negative training labels.
sectionDiagram.caption: Combining fast analyst labels with 45-day chargeback maturity balances freshness and accuracy.

learningJourney.title: Champion-Challenger Shadow Scoring
learningJourney.purpose: Safely evaluate new GNN/XGBoost models on live traffic without risking false declines.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Champion-Challenger Shadow Scoring** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Safely evaluate new GNN/XGBoost models on live traffic without risking false declines.
explanation.core: Offline AUC doesn't capture how a model behaves on blocked transactions (selection bias). We run Challenger models in shadow mode on 100% of live traffic, logging their scores alongside the Champion, and periodically approve a 1% random exploration slice to measure true chargeback rates.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, champion-challenger shadow scoring becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production fraud scoring architecture with champion-challenger shadow logging, 1% audit holdouts, and 3DS-proxy adversarial drift detection.

learningJourney.title: Adversarial Drift & Concept-Shift Defense
learningJourney.purpose: Detect coordinated fraud-ring pivots within minutes rather than weeks.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Adversarial Drift & Concept-Shift Defense** as the intuition layer for Streaming Fraud Detection & Graph Ring Scoring: Detect coordinated fraud-ring pivots within minutes rather than weeks.
explanation.core: When fraudsters switch to a new BIN range or emulator fingerprint, chargeback labels won't arrive for weeks. Monitoring real-time score-distribution shifts (PSI), 3DS pass-rate drops, and sudden spikes in 2-hop graph density triggers immediate rule hotfixes.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, adversarial drift & concept-shift defense becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a real-time 2-hop graph lookup cap neighbor expansion (e.g., max_nodes=200) on nodes like IP addresses?

options.text: To prevent 'supernodes' like public Wi-Fi routers or carrier NAT IPs from triggering millions of traversals and timing out checkout
options.feedback: Correct! Carrier NATs and airport Wi-Fi IPs connect thousands of unrelated users; capping fan-out protects the 30ms SLA.

options.text: Because Neo4j only supports 200 total nodes in a database
options.feedback: Graph databases hold billions of nodes; the cap is for per-query tail latency.
Graph query caps are unrelated to Flink checkpoints.

options.text: To force all transactions through 3DS authentication
options.feedback: Capping supernodes avoids false positives and timeouts, rather than forcing 3DS.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Supernodes (NAT IPs, popular merchants) cause exponential traversal explosions unless bounded.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why is it dangerous to label all un-disputed transactions from the past 48 hours as negative (legitimate) training examples?

options.text: Flink RocksDB cannot store 48 hours of state
options.feedback: Offline training reads from lakehouse storage, not Flink RocksDB.

options.text: Chargebacks take 30-60 days to arrive, so recent undetected fraud would be mislabeled as legitimate
options.feedback: Correct! Immature negatives teach the model to ignore active fraud patterns.

options.text: It doubles the cost of Redis Cluster
options.feedback: Label maturity affects offline training data quality, not Redis cost.

options.text: It breaks Protobuf serialization in the Payment Gateway
options.feedback: Labeling logic has no impact on wire serialization.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: A 45-day maturity window (supplemented by analyst reviews) prevents un-reported fraud from polluting negative labels.

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the primary benefit of a 3-way Decision Gate (Approve / Step-Up 3DS / Hard Block) over a binary Approve/Block gate?

options.text: It removes the need for XGBoost or GNN models
options.feedback: The 3-way gate relies on calibrated risk scores from the ensemble.

options.text: It reduces false declines on borderline transactions by shifting liability via 3DS verification
options.feedback: Correct! Borderline scores get a cryptographic challenge instead of an outright decline, saving legitimate revenue.

options.text: It guarantees zero chargebacks on all approved transactions
options.feedback: No system can guarantee zero chargebacks.

options.text: It eliminates network latency between the Payment Gateway and Kafka
options.feedback: Decision routing happens after scoring, not at network ingress.

knowledgeChecks.explanation: Step-Up 3DS resolves mid-risk ambiguity without sacrificing good customer conversions.

beginner.summary: Streaming fraud detection checks transaction speed and hidden device connections in milliseconds to stop stolen cards before money moves.
beginner.keyTakeaway: When durability and read throughput pull in opposite directions, velocity counters catch individual card-testing bursts, while 2-hop Device/IP/Card graph lookups expose coordinated fraud rings rotating stolen credentials.
beginner.byteSummary:
When you swipe a card, a fraud engine has 30ms to decide if it's really you.

It checks how fast the card is being used and whether the device is linked to known scammers, then approves, asks for 3DS verification, or blocks.
